title: Silte Dabo Firfir
localName: ሲልጤ ዳቦ ፍርፍር — Silte Dabo Firfir
community: Silte people — the bread-eating culture of the Silte Zone
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Silte Dabo Firfir — torn day-old Silte flatbread tossed with eggs, berbere, kibbeh, and onion. The Silte version of firfir — using their distinctive wheat flatbread rather than injera. The Silte Zone of central Ethiopia is known for its unique flatbread tradition.
longDesc: The Silte are a Muslim people closely related to the Gurage, living in the Silte Zone south of Addis Ababa. Their flatbread tradition differs from both injera and standard kita — the Silte Dabo Firfir uses this bread torn and tossed with eggs and berbere.
ingredients: 3 pieces day-old Silte flatbread or kita (ETH007) — torn
steps: Heat kibbeh. Cook onion until golden.
Add torn bread. Toss to coat.
Add beaten eggs. Scramble with the bread — 3—4 minutes.
chefTips: Day-old bread holds together better than fresh.
The eggs are added at the end and scrambled through.
commonMistakes: Fresh bread — too soft, becomes mushy.
culturalNote: Silte Dabo Firfir is the breakfast that uses yesterday's bread — the Silte people's version of the universal Ethiopian firfir tradition, adapted to their specific flatbread culture.
